Step 1: Extract relevant information.
- Item 1 (chat dated 2023-01-15): the user watched the College Football National Championship game (Georgia beat Alabama 33-18) with family "yesterday," so about January 14, 2023. (The actual game was Jan 9, 2023, but the user's account places it in mid-January, and it is a January event either way.)
- Item 2 (chat dated 2023-01-22): the user watched the Chiefs beat the Bills in the NFL Divisional Round "last weekend" at Mike's place, so about January 14-15, 2023 (the actual game was Jan 22, 2023, but the user says it was last weekend).
- Other items (the team-building event, autocross participation, and volleyball practice) are not sports events the user watched.

Step 2: Order them.
- The championship game was described on Jan 15 as "yesterday," so Jan 14.
- The Chiefs-Bills game was described on Jan 22 as "last weekend," so Jan 14-15 or so (Saturday/Sunday before Jan 22).
- These are close. Since the championship game is said to be "yesterday" on Jan 15 (Saturday, Jan 14), and the Chiefs game was "last weekend" relative to Jan 22 (weekend of Jan 14-15), the timing overlaps. The most defensible reading is that the college football game came first (Jan 14, Saturday), and the Chiefs game on the weekend of Jan 14-15 came at the same time or after it (Sunday, Jan 15).

Answer: First, the College Football National Championship game (Georgia vs. Alabama, which the user watched with family at home). Second, the NFL Divisional Round game (Chiefs vs. Bills, which the user watched at Mike's place).
